title: 2001 HMMT February General Round 2 Problem 8
statement: A point on a circle inscribed in a square is 1 and 2 units from the two closest sides of the square. Find the area of the square.

solutions.text: Call the point in question \(A\), the center of the circle \(O\), and its radius \(r\). Consider a right triangle \(B O A\) with hypotenuse \(O A\) : \(O A\) has length \(r\), and \(B O\) and \(B A\) have lengths \(r-1\) and \(r-2\). By the Pythagorean theorem, \((r-1)^{2}+(r-2)^{2}=r^{2} \Rightarrow\) \(r^{2}-6 r+5=0 \Rightarrow r=5\) since \(r>4\). The area of the square is \((2 r)^{2}=100\).
